title: PIVOT Operator
description: Learn how to use the SQL Server PIVOT operator to convert rows into columns for cross-tabulation reports.

data.text: The PIVOT operator rotates a table-valued expression, turning unique values from one column into multiple columns in the output. It also performs aggregations on any remaining column values.
Consider the production.products and production.categories tables from the sample database. The following query counts the number of products in each category.

data.title: Product Count by Category
data.content: Counts the number of products per product category.
data.code:
SELECT
    category_name,
    COUNT(product_id) AS product_count
FROM
    production.products p
    INNER JOIN production.categories c
        ON c.category_id = p.category_id
GROUP BY
    category_name;

data.alt: PIVOT GROUP BY with COUNT example output

data.text: Our goal is to transform the category names from rows into columns, with the product count for each category as the values. The PIVOT operator makes this possible.
To create a pivot table, follow these steps:

items: Select a base dataset for pivoting.
Create a temporary result using a derived table or common table expression (CTE).
Apply the PIVOT operator to rotate the rows into columns.

data.title: PIVOT with COUNT
data.content: Converts category names into columns with product counts.
data.code:
SELECT * FROM
(
    SELECT
        category_name,
        product_id
    FROM
        production.products p
        INNER JOIN production.categories c
            ON c.category_id = p.category_id
) t
PIVOT(
    COUNT(product_id)
    FOR category_name IN (
        [Children Bicycles],
        [Comfort Bicycles],
        [Cruisers Bicycles],
        [Cyclocross Bicycles],
        [Electric Bikes],
        [Mountain Bikes],
        [Road Bikes])
) AS pivot_table;

data.alt: SQL Server PIVOT operator example output

data.text: Adding the model year column to the base data creates row groups in the pivot table, allowing you to see counts by category and model year.

data.title: PIVOT with Model Year
data.content: Adds model year as an additional grouping dimension.
data.code:
SELECT * FROM
(
    SELECT
        category_name,
        product_id,
        model_year
    FROM
        production.products p
        INNER JOIN production.categories c
            ON c.category_id = p.category_id
) t
PIVOT(
    COUNT(product_id)
    FOR category_name IN (
        [Children Bicycles],
        [Comfort Bicycles],
        [Cruisers Bicycles],
        [Cyclocross Bicycles],
        [Electric Bikes],
        [Mountain Bikes],
        [Road Bikes])
) AS pivot_table;

data.alt: SQL Server PIVOT operator with model year example output

data.text: When category names change frequently, hardcoding them in the PIVOT clause is not ideal. You can use dynamic SQL to build the pivot query automatically.

data.title: Dynamic PIVOT with sp_executesql
data.content: Generates category names dynamically and executes the pivot query.

data.title: PIVOT Operator Key Points
points: PIVOT rotates rows into columns for cross-tabulation reports.
Use a derived table or CTE as the base dataset for pivoting.
The IN clause lists the values that become column headers.
Dynamic SQL with sp_executesql allows the pivot columns to adapt to data changes.
